general.label: General
general.description: When Loupist runs, and what leaves this Mac.
general.keywords: general menu bar background running privacy notice about telemetry keychain
general.keepRunning: Keep running in the menu bar
general.keepRunningDescription: Scheduled tasks and Watching run only while Loupist is open or in the menu bar.
general.keepRunningAutomatic: Not chosen yet. Loupist turns this on when you start a briefing or Watching.
general.saveFailed: Couldn't change this setting. Try again.
general.privacyStays: Stays on this Mac: chats, sources, Map, Lens, Journal and holdings, in each Loupist's folder. No Loupist account, no sync.
general.privacyProvider: Goes to your AI provider: your messages, and the sources and saved notes an answer or background reading uses.
general.privacyDataSources: Goes to data sources: names and tickers you follow or ask about, and wallet addresses you add. Holdings quantities and values never leave this Mac.
general.privacyWeb: Goes to the web: pages your Loupist opens and searches it runs. A connection you add yourself gets what its tools ask for.
general.privacyMakers: Loupist's makers receive nothing: no analytics or telemetry. The app checks GitHub for a signed update about once a day, sooner after a failed check.
general.privacyKeys: Keys and sign-ins: data-connection keys in the macOS Keychain; AI sign-ins and keys in Loupist's private app folder on this Mac.

skill-creator.name: Skill Creator
skill-creator.description: Create or improve a reusable workflow with instructions, references, scripts, or templates.

skill-installer.name: Skill Installer
skill-installer.description: Find, inspect, and add skills from GitHub, ZIP packages, or local folders.

dividend-income.name: Dividend income
dividend-income.description: Check how safe and how steady a company's dividend looks from its history, payout on earnings and free cash flow, cuts, growth, yield and record dates. Use when someone asks whether a dividend is safe, sustainable or growing; skip a single dividend-amount lookup.

fund-compare.name: Fund comparison
fund-compare.description: Compare ETFs or funds side by side on cost, size, age, holdings overlap and returns over one shared window. Use when choosing between funds or checking whether two funds hold the same things; skip a single fund quote.

why-it-moved.name: Why it moved
why-it-moved.description: Explain why a stock, fund or index moved on a day or over a period, keeping the measured move, reported reasons and inference apart. Use for questions like why something rose or fell; skip a plain price lookup.

goal-math.name: Goal math
goal-math.description: Do the arithmetic for a savings or investing goal, such as what regular saving could grow to, what a target needs each period, or how regular investing in an asset would have turned out. Use when someone gives an amount, a period or a target; skip choosing products for them.

research.name: Research
research.description: Investigate a financial question across sources or challenge an investment thesis with evidence, counterevidence, and observable catalysts. Use for multi-step research; answer isolated facts and calculations directly.

valuation.name: Valuation
valuation.description: Build or audit an intrinsic valuation model, cash-flow forecast, sum-of-parts valuation, or sensitivity range. Use for a substantive valuation workflow; skip a quote lookup or an isolated arithmetic question.

comparison.name: Peer comparison
comparison.description: Build a peer-company comparison or trading-comparables analysis, including metric alignment, peer selection, and valuation distributions. Use for substantive comparisons; skip a single-company lookup or a simple ratio.

filings.name: Filings and earnings
filings.description: Analyze filings, financial statements, earnings releases, guidance changes, or earnings quality, including a Korean company's capital decisions, ownership reports, dividends and investor flows. Use for a document-based financial review; skip a price lookup or an isolated calculation with complete supplied inputs.

rule-test.name: Backtesting
rule-test.description: Design, implement, or audit a historical strategy test, screening rule, rebalance simulation, or parameter search. Use for backtesting workflows; skip an isolated return calculation.

portfolio-risk.name: Portfolio and risk
portfolio-risk.description: Review portfolio exposure, diversification, drawdown, covariance, tail risk, stress scenarios, risk contribution, or constrained allocation models. Use for a portfolio analysis workflow; skip a simple weighted-return calculation.

events-stats.name: Events and statistics
events-stats.description: Design or audit an event study, regression, factor analysis, hypothesis test, or statistical interpretation of market moves. Use for inference workflows; answer a fully specified one-step statistic directly.

data-analysis.name: Dataset analysis
data-analysis.description: Profile, clean, join, transform, or audit financial datasets and reproducible local analyses. Use for multi-step data work or data-quality problems; skip a simple calculation over complete supplied values.

pdf.name: PDF
pdf.description: Read, extract, edit, assemble, fill, or generate PDF files, including scanned pages and financial tables. Use when PDF structure, OCR, forms, or page layout matter.

documents.name: Word documents
documents.description: Create, inspect, or edit Word documents and templates (.docx/.dotx), including tables, styles, headers, citations, and revisions. Use for Word-file deliverables; plain chat prose needs no document workflow.

spreadsheets.name: Spreadsheets
spreadsheets.description: Read, build, or edit spreadsheet files such as .xlsx and .xlsm, including formulas, financial models, formatting, and charts. Use when workbook behavior matters; ordinary CSV analysis can use data-analysis.

presentations.name: Presentations
presentations.description: Read, create, or edit PowerPoint decks and templates (.pptx/.potx), including financial charts, tables, speaker notes, and slide layouts. Use for a deck deliverable or an existing presentation.

world.name: Map
world.description: Use when investigating what this Loupist already knows about entities, events, and their relationships, or when organizing source-grounded knowledge in the Map.

lens.name: Lens
lens.description: Use when the user teaches or corrects a reusable method, rule, convention, or preference, or when inspecting this Loupist's perspective and methods. Skip a one-off.

journal.name: Journal
journal.description: Record your own judgments and revisit optional checks with facts.

visualize.name: Visualize
visualize.description: Create or revise a Loupist chart, diagram, or visual export. Use when a visual helps answer the question or the user requests one; simple facts and short tables can remain text.
